transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. I came in because... well, what started as just trying to eat cleaner for the lieutenant track has turned into something else. 

I've been cutting my meals down a lot. It's gotten to the point where I'm pretty much just having black coffee, a protein shake, and a small dinner. And I'm doing that even on shift days at the firehouse, when I know for a fact I've burned way more than what I'm taking in.
Have you experienced any episodes where you feel you lose control over your eating and consume an unusually large amount of food in a short period?

No, not at all. I haven't had anything like that happen. It's... it's really the exact opposite for me. I don't ever eat a large amount of food at once, and I definitely don't feel like I lose control and overeat. I pretty much just stick strictly to the small amounts I mentioned.
Do you engage in any behaviors like self-induced vomiting or the misuse of laxatives or diuretics to influence your weight?

No, I don't do anything like that. I've never made myself throw up, and I definitely don't take laxatives or water pills or anything to lose weight. I just... I just strictly limit what I eat in the first place, so I don't really feel the need to do any of that.
How would you describe your feelings about your current body weight or shape?

Well, I'd say I tie a lot of how I feel about myself to how I look. Like, when I look in the mirror before work, I'm really checking to see if my waist and face look sharp enough. If they don't... if I feel like I'm carrying extra weight, it really messes with my head. It actually affects how confident and command-ready I feel for my shift that day. I just feel like I need to look a certain way to be at my best.
Could you tell me what your current height and weight are?

I don't have the exact numbers for you right now, to be honest. But I know it's down. My gear and my station clothes hang a lot looser on me now than they used to. We actually had a fitness review at the firehouse recently, and they flagged my weight as being too low for my build. But... I don't know, even after they told me that, part of me still feels like I should keep trimming down a little more.
Could you provide an estimate of your current height and weight so I can better understand the extent of your weight loss?

I honestly don't have a good estimate to give you. I haven't actually stepped on a scale to look at the numbers in a long time. I know I'm pretty average height, but as far as my weight goes... I just really don't know. Like I said, I just go by how my uniform fits and what I see in the mirror. So I couldn't even give you a rough guess right now.
When you think about the possibility of gaining weight or not being able to keep your weight down, how does that make you feel?

The idea of gaining weight... it honestly terrifies me. Even just thinking about it makes me anxious. Like, if I ever do check my weight and the scale is up even a pound—maybe after a big meal at the station or just drinking extra water—I get this tight feeling of panic. It feels like I've completely blown it. I just immediately start worrying that people are going to see me as soft or out of control, and I can't handle that.
